claims.observed_behavior: Every lifecycle refresh calls rebuildFilesIndex. The rebuild recursively enumerates the project and stats every indexed file; validation enumerates the project again.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C07 requires incremental changed-path indexing and forbids rebuilding the files index after every small transition.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/local-state-indexes.test.ts:989-1138 covers validity, freshness, and exclusions; the focused 44-test state/index run passed. No transition-cost or tree-size performance test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Create a large project tree, run new/start/evidence/done, and trace repeated readdirSync/statSync calls. A single lifecycle transition is sufficient to trigger a full scan.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C07: maintain changed-path/source-generation metadata and refresh only the affected index surfaces.

claims.observed_behavior: Different sessions hold different locks while both can rebuild the shared files.json. The write is atomic, but freshness uses only generated_at versus current source mtimes, so an older scan that finishes later can overwrite a newer scan and appear fresh.
claims.intended_contract: Shared indexes must serialize or compare generations so concurrent lifecycle operations cannot publish incomplete fresh-looking state.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/local-state-indexes.test.ts:571-666 proves concurrent scoped workbench-index merges only; no concurrent files-index writer or source-generation test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Start two lifecycle processes for different sessions; delay the first scan, create a file, let the second scan commit, then let the first commit. Check that files.json can omit the file while validateFilesIndex returns ok.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04/C07: add a shared files-index lock or source-set generation/CAS and reject stale publish attempts.

claims.observed_behavior: Workbench events use a session lock and append to the shared log. Telemetry explicitly takes no lock; standalone writers rely on append-only writes, with no global sequence or fsync. Same-session lifecycle ordering is covered, but cross-session ordering and crash durability are not.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C04 requires durable coordinated events, with a single global writer/sequence/fsync path or an equivalent durable append-only design.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/telemetry-command.test.ts:45-62 uses sequential process spawns; cli/tests/workbench-lifecycle.test.ts:1306-1371 covers same-session evidence serialization. No different-session global-writer or crash-durability test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Spawn telemetry and workbench writers for two sessions concurrently, terminate one during append, and inspect ordering, durability after restart, and absence of a global sequence.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: centralize the shared event append/sequence path or document and test a durable equivalent with fsync at critical boundaries.

claims.observed_behavior: readTelemetryEvents JSON-parses every non-empty line and throws on one malformed row. Workbench lifecycle indexing catches the same parse failure and silently continues, so the same corrupt log is fatal to one reader and incomplete to another.
claims.intended_contract: Corrupt durable event input must surface as an integrity failure, not be silently skipped or projected as complete state.
claims.test_coverage: The focused telemetry and index suites passed, but no malformed events.jsonl fixture exists. The bounded probe with one valid row plus not-json produced SyntaxError from readTelemetryEvents.
claims.repro_candidate: Append a malformed line between two valid lifecycle events; telemetry query throws while rebuildWorkBenchIndex ignores the line and may omit lifecycle state.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: use one strict event parser, report corruption with line identity, and quarantine or explicitly classify incomplete projections.

claims.observed_behavior: The non-shell command parser treats every backslash as an escape and removes it. The bounded runVerification probe passed only when C:\tmp\foo was reduced to the eight-character C:tmpfoo argument.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C07 requires structured argv handling and preservation of Windows path separators.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/workbench-lifecycle.test.ts covers shell and non-shell execution paths, but no test contains a Windows drive path or asserts argv backslashes.
claims.repro_candidate: Run workbench done with --test node -e ... C:\tmp\foo; the child receives C:tmpfoo in the non-shell route.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C07: replace splitCommandLine with an explicit argv contract/parser that preserves literal backslashes and quoted Windows paths.

claims.observed_behavior: Before bootstrap mutation, snapshotTarget recursively copies the entire existing target and rollback recursively copies it back. The transaction has no touched-path filter, so .git, node_modules, and untouched assets are included in the snapshot I/O.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C07 requires bootstrap snapshots limited to touched paths; F22-C03 requires staged, atomic, recoverable bootstrap behavior.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/bootstrap.test.ts:309-361 verifies exact-tree rollback after injected failures; no fixture asserts exclusion of .git, node_modules, or untouched large assets and no snapshot-cost bound exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Place a large node_modules/.git/assets tree in the target, inject failAfterTemplateWrite, and measure that snapshot/restore traverses the complete tree.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C03/C07: build a touched-path snapshot manifest and preserve a recoverable fallback only for paths that the operation can mutate.

claims.observed_behavior: Workbench-index writers serialize under a shared session lock, but writeSnapshot truncates and writes the final JSON path directly. Readers do not take that lock and return null on a transient parse failure, so a reader can observe an incomplete snapshot during a valid writer commit.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C07 requires every index to be written atomically and readers to distinguish invalid/incomplete state from fresh state.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/local-state-indexes.test.ts:571-666 covers concurrent writer merge preservation and the focused index suite passed; no concurrent reader/torn-write test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Loop loadWorkBenchIndexSnapshot while another process rebuilds a large index; observe null/invalid reads or a transient missing snapshot during direct writeFileSync.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C03/C07: use temp-file plus rename/fsync for the workbench index and classify any read failure as an integrity finding.

claims.observed_behavior: newWorkstream creates the final session directory, writes plan, task, log, evidence, and active pointer one at a time, then writes auxiliary events, pending-spec state, and indexes. There is no staging/promote or rollback for failure during initial artifact creation.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C03 requires workstreams to be created in staging and promoted atomically; .active_session must change only after commit.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/workbench-lifecycle.test.ts:166-185 covers successful artifact creation; fault tests cover auxiliary failures after creation, not failure between initial atomicWriteText calls.
claims.repro_candidate: Inject an error on the second initial artifact write or make the active-pointer path unavailable; inspect the partially created session directory and pointer state.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C03: write the complete workstream into a staging directory, validate it, then rename/promote and update the pointer as the commit boundary.

claims.observed_behavior: resolvePendingSpec holds only the governance lock while rewriting plan/task frontmatter and the pending index. runStartCommand checks pending state before startTask acquires the session lock. The two operations can make a stale gate decision or race on the same markdown files.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C02/C03 requires governance resolution and lifecycle mutation to share a safe lock domain or revalidate authority at commit time.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/workbench-lifecycle.test.ts:470-491 proves the sequential pending-spec gate; cli/tests/spec-gate-system.test.ts:248-265 proves rollback after injected failure. No concurrent resolve/start test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Run governance resolve-spec and workbench start concurrently for the same pending session; pause after frontmatter read and inspect whether start commits against the pre-resolution gate or resolution loses task metadata.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C02/C03: coordinate governance and session locks, or use a version/CAS check and revalidate pending status inside the lifecycle commit.

claims.observed_behavior: runDone executes the external test outside the session lock, then recordEvidence reads the current attempt and doneTask authorizes evidence for that current attempt. A problem/restart transition during the test can therefore cause an old result to be recorded under the new attempt and authorize done.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C03 requires attempt, state, command hash, and repository fingerprint capture before execution and invalidates results when the attempt changes during execution.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/workbench-lifecycle.test.ts:2614-2645 rejects evidence recorded before a sequential restart; no test injects a restart between runVerification and recordEvidence.
claims.repro_candidate: Block runVerification with a long-lived child, transition problem then in_progress from another process, release the child, and observe evidence attempt=current followed by successful done.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C03: capture an execution token/attempt before the command, revalidate it after completion, and reject evidence when the task attempt or repository fingerprint changed.

claims.observed_behavior: The journal detects malformed rows and unmatched prepared records and fails closed, but the source exposes no recover, inspect, quarantine, or repair operation. A crash after prepared leaves the journal blocking normal reads/undo without an explicit recovery route.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C04 requires an inspectable, recoverable journal while preserving fail-closed corruption handling.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/mutation-safety.test.ts:696-742 verifies that journal corruption blocks undo without mutation; no prepared-crash recovery or quarantine test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Append a valid prepared record without a terminal record, then invoke undo/inspection paths; current loadMutationJournal reports corruption and no recovery command is available.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: add explicit read-only inspect and governed recovery/quarantine/repair commands with root identity and operator evidence.

claims.observed_behavior: appendMutationRecords serializes through the journal lock but uses appendFileSync without fsync on the journal file or containing directory. A power loss can lose a critical record after the mutation boundary returned.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C04 requires fsync for critical journal records and durable commit boundaries.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/mutation-safety.test.ts and cli/tests/update-command.test.ts cover rollback and journal failure injection, but no fsync or crash-boundary test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Instrument appendMutationRecords to terminate after appendFileSync returns and before durability; restart and compare the file mutation with the missing terminal journal state.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: fsync journal data and directory at the required commit points, with a bounded crash-recovery fixture.

claims.observed_behavior: backupPath stores an absolute path under the current project root. resolveJournalBackupPath accepts that stored absolute path, so moving the repository changes the backup location and breaks undo even though the backup is logically inside the moved repository.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C04 requires relative backup references so a repository move does not make a committed mutation non-undoable.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/mutation-safety.test.ts:170-184 and cli/tests/update-command.test.ts:874-920 check that backup paths exist; no move-root-and-undo test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Create a mutation in a temp project, move the project directory, and invoke undo; the journal still points to the old absolute backup path.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: store a validated project-relative backup path plus root identity and resolve it only under the current backup jail.

claims.observed_behavior: coordination radar maps only status=applied and skips all undo records. Actual mutation writers emit committed, noop, rolled_back, and committed undo records. Excluding noop is plausible, but committed mutations are omitted and undo does not subtract the prior path projection.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C04 requires committed mutation paths to appear in radar and committed undo to remove the corresponding paths; noop must not create a false mutation.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/local-state-indexes.test.ts:804-860 uses a synthetic applied record; no committed, noop, or undo journal fixture exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Run a real file mutation and inspect session radar; then commit undo and verify whether the original path remains projected. Run a noop and verify it remains absent.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C04: project committed records, apply inverse semantics for committed undo, and add explicit noop/undo regression fixtures.

claims.observed_behavior: OperationContext contains only caller type, trust, and interactivity. Lifecycle mutation checks task existence/state but no actor, lease, or owner binding; radar treats generic owner as a warning. A trusted local caller can mutate a task owned by another actor.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C05 requires actor/lease validation on every mutation and owner isolation rather than warning-only metadata.
claims.test_coverage: Focused lifecycle and radar tests cover restricted callers and missing-owner warnings, but no owner mismatch, actor identity, lease, or takeover denial test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Create an in-progress task with owner alice and invoke a trusted local mutation using actor bob or no actor; current state checks allow it.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C05: add actor/lease identity to operation context and require a matching owner/lease or explicit governed takeover for every mutation.

claims.observed_behavior: The canonical resolver prioritizes explicit, AFOL_SESSION, context, and global active session, but its options have no caller/actor binding and global fallback defaults on outside CI. Agent/remote callers are not intrinsically prohibited from resolving the active pointer through this API.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C05 prohibits global session fallback for agent/remote callers and binds resolution to actor/worktree authority.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/session-command.test.ts covers resolver priority and CI global-fallback denial, but no agent/remote resolver test passes caller identity or proves active-pointer denial outside CI.
claims.repro_candidate: Call resolveSession with no explicit/env/context session while an active pointer exists and a simulated agent/remote operation; the API has no actor input and returns source=global outside CI.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C05: make SessionResolver actor-aware and default-deny global fallback for restricted callers, with explicit takeover semantics.

claims.observed_behavior: status reads .active_session directly, state resolves explicit session or .active_session, and catchup does the same. These paths ignore AFOL_SESSION and session-context bindings and therefore do not use the canonical resolver.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C05 requires status, state, lifecycle, and context to share one SessionResolver with consistent fallback rules.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/status.test.ts:265-319 covers active-pointer status and cli/tests/session-command.test.ts covers the resolver in isolation; no integration test binds a context/env session and checks status/state/catchup selection.
claims.repro_candidate: Bind session B, leave .active_session at session A, set AFOL_SESSION=B, and run status/state/catchup without --session; the direct readers select A.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C05: route all session selection through one resolver and add context/env versus active-pointer integration tests.

claims.observed_behavior: Malformed adapter config is read as enabled and writeClaudeAdapterEnabled replaces malformed content with a new minimal config. The writer uses direct writeFileSync without a lock/CAS; disable/enable writes config before archive/restore, so a later failure leaves a split state.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires fail-closed corruption handling, CAS/locks, and transactional adapter config/artifact updates.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/adapter-command.test.ts:50-121,135-179 covers valid toggles, archive/restore, and symlink rejection; the malformed-config probe returned enabled=true and confirmed overwrite. No concurrency or fault-between-config-and-artifact test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Write invalid JSON to .afol/config.json, call adapter disable, and inspect that the invalid config is silently replaced; inject archive failure after the config write to leave artifacts/config divergent.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: fail closed on malformed config, lock/CAS the config, and stage config plus artifact changes with rollback.

claims.observed_behavior: readMemory returns null for malformed content. addEntry treats null as a missing empty memory and rewrites it with the new entry; updateEntry is an unlocked read-modify-write. Corruption is therefore overwritten and concurrent additions can lose data.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires memory corruption to fail closed and concurrent memory writes to preserve both additions through locking/CAS.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/memory-crud.test.ts:113-182 covers valid entries, duplicates, and status updates; the corruption probe showed corruptMarkerPreserved=false after addEntry. No malformed-store or concurrent-writer test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Write invalid memory markdown, call addEntry, and compare the file before/after; start two addEntry processes against one valid file to expose read-modify-write loss.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: distinguish missing from corrupt memory, fail closed, and use a memory lock plus content hash CAS for writes.

claims.observed_behavior: Library topic mutations read/clone/write without a per-topic lock or CAS. Invalid topic content parses as null; rebuildLibraryIndex filters null topics out, silently publishing an incomplete index instead of an integrity failure.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires per-topic locking/CAS and corruption to be surfaced before library indexes are rebuilt.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/library-system.test.ts:71-330 covers valid CRUD, duplicate slug, claim validation, and index creation; no corrupt-topic fixture or concurrent addSource/addClaim test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Corrupt one topic markdown, call rebuildLibraryIndex, and observe the topic disappear. Run two addClaim processes against one topic and compare retained claims.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: add per-topic locks and source hashes, and make index rebuild return an integrity error for corrupt topics.

claims.observed_behavior: createAdr scans existing files for the next ID and then writes the file without a global allocation lock. Concurrent creators can both choose the same ADR number/path and one write can replace or lose the other.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires a global lock for ADR ID allocation and distinct IDs for concurrent creates.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/spec-gate-system.test.ts:442-486 covers sequential numbering and slugification; no concurrent createAdr process test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Spawn two createAdr calls in an empty ADR directory with a barrier between nextAdrId and write; inspect duplicate ADR-001 files or a lost decision.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: serialize only ID allocation, reserve the number, and add a separate-process collision test.

claims.observed_behavior: supersedeAdr updates the old ADR with any supplied newId and does not verify that the replacement ADR exists or has an acceptable status.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires supersede to verify the replacement ADR and its status before changing the old decision.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/spec-gate-system.test.ts:507-522 covers only the valid sequential old/new case; no missing, inactive, or concurrent replacement test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Call supersedeAdr(root, "ADR-001", "ADR-999") with no replacement file; the old ADR is still marked superseded.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: validate replacement existence/status under the ADR allocation/resource lock and expose the canonical --by contract.

claims.observed_behavior: addChangelogEntry reads the entire changelog, prepends the new entry, and atomically replaces the file. There is no append-only file operation, lock, or CAS, so concurrent entries can overwrite one another despite atomic replacement.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C06 requires append-only changelog behavior and preservation of two concurrent entries.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/spec-gate-system.test.ts:538-566 covers create and sequential append; no concurrent changelog writer test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Barrier two addChangelogEntry processes after both read the same file; release both writes and verify that one heading is lost.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C06: append under a changelog lock or use a CAS loop that preserves both entries and validates the resulting document.

claims.observed_behavior: External path locks are stored under host-local tmpdir and include a host name. A lock owned by another host is never reclaimed, so separate WSL/Windows hosts do not share the lock namespace and eventually time out rather than coordinate or perform explicit takeover.
claims.intended_contract: F22-C05 requires explicit one-host-per-worktree isolation/takeover rules and separate Windows/WSL worktrees; the current host-local lock boundary must be explicit and fail-closed.
claims.test_coverage: cli/tests/session-lock.test.ts:260-306,393-462 covers same-host stale/live behavior and symlink-equivalent keys; no foreign-host/shared-lock-root or explicit takeover test exists.
claims.repro_candidate: Create an external lock file with host=other-host for the same canonical path and call withExternalPathLock; it refuses reclaim and times out. Repeat from Windows/WSL to show separate tmpdir namespaces.
claims.recommended_slice: F22-C05: document and enforce the one-host boundary with an explicit takeover/lease protocol, or use a shared project lock root when cross-host coordination is supported.
